title: OSHA crane inspections practice questions
description: Free OSHA crane inspection practice questions on 29 CFR 1926.1412: triggers, who inspects, deficiencies and records. Each answer quotes the rule.

questions.question: 1926.1412 gives the shift inspection to a competent person. Besides being capable of identifying existing and predictable hazards, what does the 1926.1401 definition of a competent person include?

options.A: A license as a registered professional engineer
options.B: At least five years of crane operating experience
options.C: Authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate those hazards
options.D: A current crane operator certification

questions.explanation: A competent person is "one who is capable of identifying existing and predictable hazards in the surroundings or working conditions which are unsanitary, hazardous, or dangerous to employees, and who has authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them."
questions.evidence: and who has authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them.

questions.question: Most inspections in 1926.1412 must be done by a qualified person. How does 1926.1401 define a qualified person?

options.A: A person who, by possession of a recognized degree, certificate, or professional standing, or by extensive knowledge, training and experience, successfully demonstrated the ability to solve/resolve problems relating to the subject matter, the work, or the project
options.B: Any person the employer names in writing as the crane inspector, with no other condition
options.C: A person who has operated the same model of equipment for at least one year
options.D: A person employed by the equipment manufacturer

questions.explanation: A qualified person is one "who, by possession of a recognized degree, certificate, or professional standing, or who by extensive knowledge, training and experience, successfully demonstrated the ability to solve/resolve problems relating to the subject matter, the work, or the project."
questions.evidence: Qualified person means a person who, by possession of a recognized degree, certificate, or professional standing, or who by extensive knowledge, training and experience, successfully demonstrated the ability to solve/resolve problems relating to the subject matter, the work, or the project.

questions.question: Equipment has had a modification that affects its safe operation. Who must inspect it under 1926.1412(a)(1), and at what point?

options.A: A competent person, at the start of the next shift the equipment is used
options.B: The operator, during the first lift after the modification
options.C: A registered professional engineer, within 30 days after the equipment returns to service
options.D: A qualified person, after the modifications have been completed and prior to initial use

questions.explanation: Such equipment "must be inspected by a qualified person after such modifications/additions have been completed, prior to initial use."
questions.evidence: must be inspected by a qualified person after such modifications/additions have been completed, prior to initial use.

questions.question: Besides assuring the work was done in accordance with the approval obtained under 1926.1434, what must the inspection of modified equipment include under 1926.1412(a)(1)?

options.A: A review by a representative of the equipment manufacturer
options.B: Functional testing of the equipment
options.C: Complete disassembly of the boom
options.D: A written report sent to OSHA

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a)(1)(ii) states: "The inspection must include functional testing of the equipment." Under (a)(2), the equipment "must not be used until an inspection under this paragraph demonstrates that the requirements of paragraph (a)(1)(i) of this section have been met."
questions.evidence: The inspection must include functional testing of the equipment.

questions.question: After a repair that relates to safe operation, manufacturer equipment criteria for the repair are unavailable. What must the qualified person determine under 1926.1412(b)(1)(ii)(A)?

options.A: Whether OSHA must approve the repair before use
options.B: Whether the criteria for the most similar model may be used
options.C: Whether the equipment must be permanently removed from service
options.D: Whether a registered professional engineer (RPE) is needed to develop criteria for the repair/adjustment

questions.explanation: "Where manufacturer equipment criteria are unavailable or inapplicable, the qualified person must" "Determine if a registered professional engineer (RPE) is needed to develop criteria for the repair/adjustment." If an RPE is needed, the employer must ensure the criteria "are developed by an RPE."
questions.evidence: Determine if a registered professional engineer (RPE) is needed to develop criteria for the repair/adjustment.

questions.question: What must the functional testing in an inspection of repaired/adjusted equipment cover under 1926.1412(b)(1)(iii)?

options.A: The repaired/adjusted parts and other components that may be affected by the repair/adjustment
options.B: Only the single part that was repaired
options.C: Only the load hook and its latch
options.D: Only the controls in the operator cab

questions.explanation: "The inspection must include functional testing of the repaired/adjusted parts and other components that may be affected by the repair/adjustment."
questions.evidence: The inspection must include functional testing of the repaired/adjusted parts and other components that may be affected by the repair/adjustment.

questions.question: Upon completion of assembly, what must the qualified person's inspection assure under 1926.1412(c)(1)?

options.A: That the operator holds a current certification
options.B: That a trial lift at rated capacity has been made
options.C: That the equipment is configured in accordance with manufacturer equipment criteria
options.D: That the monthly inspection record is on site

questions.explanation: "Upon completion of assembly, the equipment must be inspected by a qualified person to assure that it is configured in accordance with manufacturer equipment criteria." 1926.1401 defines equipment criteria as "instructions, recommendations, limitations and specifications."
questions.evidence: Upon completion of assembly, the equipment must be inspected by a qualified person to assure that it is configured in accordance with manufacturer equipment criteria.

questions.question: Manufacturer equipment criteria for a configuration are unavailable, and the qualified person decides that a registered professional engineer is not needed. Who must the employer ensure develops the configuration criteria under 1926.1412(c)(2)(i)?

options.A: The equipment operator
options.B: The qualified person
options.C: The signal person
options.D: The competent person who does the shift inspection

questions.explanation: "If an RPE is not needed, the employer must ensure that the criteria are developed by the qualified person. If an RPE is needed, the employer must ensure that they are developed by an RPE." Under (c)(3), the equipment "must not be used until an inspection under this paragraph demonstrates that the equipment is configured in accordance with the applicable criteria."
questions.evidence: If an RPE is not needed, the employer must ensure that the criteria are developed by the qualified person.

questions.question: Who does 1926.1412(d)(1) assign to the each-shift visual inspection, and when must it be completed?

options.A: A competent person begins it prior to each shift the equipment will be used, and it must be completed before or during that shift
options.B: A qualified person begins it at the end of the previous shift, and it must be completed before the next shift
options.C: The operator does it once a week, before the first shift of the week
options.D: A registered professional engineer does it before each shift, and it must be documented

questions.explanation: "A competent person must begin a visual inspection prior to each shift the equipment will be used, which must be completed before or during that shift."
questions.evidence: A competent person must begin a visual inspection prior to each shift the equipment will be used, which must be completed before or during that shift.

questions.question: Under 1926.1412(d)(1), when does the shift inspection require taking apart equipment components or booming down?

options.A: At every shift inspection
options.B: Only on equipment with a boom longer than 100 feet
options.C: Only when a qualified person is present
options.D: When the results of the visual inspection or trial operation indicate that further investigation necessitating it is needed

questions.explanation: "Taking apart equipment components and booming down is not required as part of this inspection unless the results of the visual inspection or trial operation indicate that further investigation necessitating taking apart equipment components or booming down is needed."
questions.evidence: Taking apart equipment components and booming down is not required as part of this inspection unless the results of the visual inspection or trial operation indicate that further investigation necessitating taking apart equipment components or booming down is needed.

questions.question: The shift inspection finds a deficiency in one of the items in 1926.1412(d)(1)(i) through (xiii). What does paragraph (d)(2) require?

options.A: The deficiency is written down and corrected at the next monthly inspection
options.B: The operator decides at the end of the shift whether to report it
options.C: An immediate determination by the competent person as to whether the deficiency constitutes a safety hazard; if it does, the equipment is taken out of service until it has been corrected
options.D: The manufacturer must be notified before the next lift

questions.explanation: "An immediate determination must be made by the competent person as to whether the deficiency constitutes a safety hazard. If the deficiency is determined to constitute a safety hazard, the equipment must be taken out of service until it has been corrected."
questions.evidence: If the deficiency is determined to constitute a safety hazard, the equipment must be taken out of service until it has been corrected.

questions.question: Under 1926.1412(e)(3)(i), what information must be documented for the monthly inspection, and by whom must it be maintained?

options.A: Only the date of the inspection, kept by the equipment operator
options.B: The items checked and the results of the inspection, and the name and signature of the person who conducted the inspection and the date, maintained by the employer that conducts the inspection
options.C: A photograph of each item checked, kept by the equipment manufacturer
options.D: The operator's certification number, kept by the controlling contractor

questions.explanation: "The following information must be documented and maintained by the employer that conducts the inspection: (A) The items checked and the results of the inspection. (B) The name and signature of the person who conducted the inspection and the date."
questions.evidence: The following information must be documented and maintained by the employer that conducts the inspection:

questions.question: What minimum retention period does 1926.1412(e)(3)(ii) set for the monthly inspection document?

options.A: One month
options.B: Two weeks
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: Three months

questions.explanation: "This document must be retained for a minimum of three months."
questions.evidence: This document must be retained for a minimum of three months.

questions.question: In the annual/comprehensive inspection, the qualified person finds a deficiency that is not yet a safety hazard but needs to be monitored. What must the employer ensure under 1926.1412(f)(6)?

options.A: That the deficiency is checked in the monthly inspections
options.B: That the equipment is taken out of service until the deficiency is corrected
options.C: That a registered professional engineer certifies the equipment within 30 days
options.D: That the deficiency is checked again at the next annual inspection only

questions.explanation: "If the qualified person determines that, though not presently a safety hazard, the deficiency needs to be monitored, the employer must ensure that the deficiency is checked in the monthly inspections."
questions.evidence: If the qualified person determines that, though not presently a safety hazard, the deficiency needs to be monitored, the employer must ensure that the deficiency is checked in the monthly inspections.

questions.question: The qualified person determines during the annual/comprehensive inspection that a deficiency is a safety hazard. Under 1926.1412(f)(5), what is the exception to taking the equipment out of service until it is corrected?

options.A: When the operator agrees to work at reduced speed
options.B: When the next annual inspection is less than 30 days away
options.C: When temporary alternative measures are implemented as specified in § 1926.1416(d) or § 1926.1435(e)
options.D: When lifts are kept under half of rated capacity

questions.explanation: The equipment "must be taken out of service until it has been corrected, except when temporary alternative measures are implemented as specified in § 1926.1416(d) or § 1926.1435(e)."
questions.evidence: except when temporary alternative measures are implemented as specified in § 1926.1416(d) or § 1926.1435(e).

questions.question: What does 1926.1412(f)(2) say about disassembly for the annual/comprehensive inspection of equipment structure, sheaves, drums, brakes and the other listed items?

options.A: Disassembly is never part of the inspection
options.B: Disassembly is required, as necessary, to complete the inspection
options.C: Complete disassembly of the equipment is required every year
options.D: Disassembly is required only if a registered professional engineer orders it

questions.explanation: "In addition, at least every 12 months, the equipment must be inspected by a qualified person. Disassembly is required, as necessary, to complete the inspection."
questions.evidence: Disassembly is required, as necessary, to complete the inspection.

questions.question: Under 1926.1412(g), the severity of use/conditions is such that there is a reasonable probability of damage or excessive wear, such as shock loading that may have exceeded rated capacity. What must happen?

options.A: The employer must stop using the equipment, and a qualified person must inspect it for structural damage to determine if it can continue to be used safely
options.B: The competent person adds the item to the next shift inspection, and work continues
options.C: The equipment may be used until the next monthly inspection
options.D: The operator must log the event, and the annual inspection is moved up by 30 days

questions.explanation: Where such conditions exist, "the employer must stop using the equipment and a qualified person must: (1) Inspect the equipment for structural damage to determine if the equipment can continue to be used safely."
questions.evidence: the employer must stop using the equipment and a qualified person must:

questions.question: Equipment has been idle for 3 months or more. What does 1926.1412(h) require before its initial use?

options.A: A shift inspection by the operator only
options.B: A trial operation observed by a signal person
options.C: An inspection by a registered professional engineer under the severe service paragraph
options.D: An inspection by a qualified person in accordance with the requirements of paragraph (e) (Monthly)

questions.explanation: "Equipment that has been idle for 3 months or more must be inspected by a qualified person in accordance with the requirements of paragraph (e) (Monthly) of this section before initial use."
questions.evidence: Equipment that has been idle for 3 months or more must be inspected by a qualified person in accordance with the requirements of paragraph (e) (Monthly) of this section before initial use.

questions.question: A manufacturer's inspection procedure relating to safe operation is more comprehensive, or has a more frequent schedule, than 1926.1412 requires. What does paragraph (j) say?

options.A: The schedule in 1926.1412 controls instead
options.B: That part of the manufacturer's procedure must be followed
options.C: The employer may choose either schedule
options.D: It is followed only if a registered professional engineer agrees

questions.explanation: Any such part of a manufacturer's procedures "that is more comprehensive or has a more frequent schedule of inspection than the requirements of this section must be followed."
questions.evidence: that is more comprehensive or has a more frequent schedule of inspection than the requirements of this section must be followed.

questions.question: Under 1926.1412(k), to whom must all documents produced under the inspection section be available, and for how long?

options.A: Only to OSHA compliance officers, for five years
options.B: Only to the equipment operator, until the next shift
options.C: To all persons who conduct inspections under this section, during the applicable document retention period
options.D: To the public on request, permanently

questions.explanation: "All documents produced under this section must be available, during the applicable document retention period, to all persons who conduct inspections under this section."
questions.evidence: All documents produced under this section must be available, during the applicable document retention period, to all persons who conduct inspections under this section.
